profile.reading:
This is the original building of xAI's Colossus supercomputer campus in South Memphis, at 3231 Riverport Road, known in permitting and advocacy records as Colossus 1 to distinguish it from a second xAI facility, Colossus 2, built afterward on the Mississippi side of the state line in Southaven and DeSoto County. The site is a former Electrolux appliance factory of about 785,000 square feet, purchased by Phoenix Investors in December 2023 for 35 million dollars. Its existing building shell and proximity to wastewater treatment infrastructure and the Mississippi River let xAI complete initial construction in roughly 122 days by the operator's own account, well under the multi-year timeline typical of new data center construction, with Dell Technologies and Supermicro widely reported to have supplied server and rack infrastructure and Nvidia the GPU hardware. xAI, incorporated by Elon Musk in March 2023, announced the Memphis project publicly on June 5, 2024, describing it as the world's largest supercomputer, brought the facility online later that year, and has used it primarily to train xAI's Grok chatbot alongside workloads tied to X, formerly Twitter, and SpaceX.

The facility's on-site gas turbine power generation has drawn sustained scrutiny from environmental and civil rights groups. In a permit application filed in January 2025, xAI disclosed 15 turbines at the site. Independent aerial imaging obtained by the Southern Environmental Law Center in April 2025 showed 35 turbines actually present, with thermal imagery that month indicating more than 30 operating simultaneously, well beyond what had been disclosed. A 60-day notice of intent to sue delivered in June 2025 reportedly prompted removal of some unpermitted turbines that same month. On July 2, 2025, the Shelby County Health Department issued an air permit authorizing 15 methane gas turbines to operate around the clock, classifying the facility as a new minor source of pollution rather than a major modification and applying a federal Clean Air Act exemption for nonroad engines to the large stationary turbines already installed on site. The Southern Environmental Law Center, the NAACP, and the local group Young Gifted and Green appealed that permit on July 16, 2025 to the Memphis and Shelby County Air Pollution Control Board, arguing the nonroad engine exemption did not legally apply and that the permitting process excluded the surrounding South Memphis and Whitehaven community, a majority Black area in zip code 38109, from any public comment period. Citing NASA satellite data, TIME reported a 3 percent rise in nitrogen dioxide, a smog-forming pollutant, in the area during the period after xAI's turbines came online, with peak pollution episodes observed in late 2024.

No formal public review process preceded the project's initial announcement, and residents in the surrounding neighborhood have described learning about the facility's scale primarily through local news coverage and independent aerial and thermal imaging investigations rather than through any community engagement process from xAI or Shelby County regulators. Because Colossus 2, the associated Mississippi facility with its own separately permitted turbine fleet, sits on a different parcel across the state line, this record's environmental findings are limited to the original Memphis building and its own Shelby County permitting history rather than the combined multi-site campus.
profile.capacity_note: No campus-wide or building-specific MW rating for this facility's gas turbines was found in primary (xAI) or non-aggregator secondary (Southern Environmental Law Center, TIME) sourcing reachable this session. Turbine counts (15 permitted per the July 2, 2025 Shelby County Health Department permit, 35 observed on site per SELC's April 2025 imaging) are documented in the reading without an associated MW figure. A 495 MW figure separately reported for the Mississippi Colossus 2 facility belongs to that distinct site and is not applied here.

reading.body:
xAI Colossus is a repurposed 785,000-square-foot appliance factory in South Memphis that the operator brought online in 2024 to train Grok and support workloads tied to X and SpaceX. The facility was built in roughly 122 days by converting an existing structure, rather than constructing a new data center from the ground up. No megawatt rating for the campus's on-site gas turbine generation has been published by the operator or verified from primary sources; the facility's power capacity and thus the scale of compute it can host remain unquantified in the public record.

The site operates with on-site methane gas turbine generation permitted at 15 units by Shelby County in July 2025, though independent aerial and thermal imaging by the Southern Environmental Law Center in April 2025 documented 35 turbines already installed on site, with more than 30 operating simultaneously. The Shelby County permit classified the facility as a new minor pollution source under a federal Clean Air Act exemption for nonroad engines; the Southern Environmental Law Center, the NAACP, and Young Gifted and Green appealed that permit in July 2025, arguing the exemption did not legally apply and that the permitting process excluded the surrounding South Memphis and Whitehaven community, a majority Black neighborhood in zip code 38109, from public comment. NASA satellite data cited by TIME showed a 3 percent rise in nitrogen dioxide in the area after the turbines came online.

In Tennessee, 23 data center facilities have been mapped and only 4 have published megawatt capacity figures, totaling 12.13 MW statewide; this campus ranks fifth among Tennessee facilities with published figures, though that ranking reflects only the four other sites with disclosed capacity, not this one. No public disclosure process preceded the project's initial announcement, and residents learned of the facility primarily through news coverage and independent investigation rather than community engagement from the operator or regulators.
